newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's worst recorded fires.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's worst recorded fires.

text.p: Following are the worst recorded fires in Hong Kong:

1918 - An estimated 600 people are killed and 400 injured at Happy Valley racecourse on Hong Kong Island at the Lunar New Year holiday when a grandstand collapses and food stall stoves are knocked over, setting bamboo matting ablaze.
1929 - A blaze in the Prince Edward Hotel in Hong Kong Island's Central district kills nine people
1947 - The Canton steamer S.S. Sai On burns on the Hong Kong dockside, killing 149 people.

1953 - On Christmas Day, the Shek Pik Mei squatter village burns down, leaving more than 60,000 homeless. There are no records of exactly how many lived there or the death toll. Hong Kong launches a drive to eliminate squatting by building cheap public housing, in which 3.5 million people now live.
1971 - Fire sweeps through the Jumbo Restaurant in Aberdeen harbour, killing 13 and injuring 42.
1972 - The cruise liner Queen Elizabeth, being used as a floating university, burns and sinks in Hong Kong harbour. There are no casualties.
1981 - Fire at a wig factory in Hong Kong Island's North Point area kills 11 workers.
1984 - Fire in the Blue Box Industrial Building in Hing Wo Street injures 44.
1986 - Fire guts Chu Ku Tsai village on Chinese Lunar New Year holiday, leaving 2,000 homeless.
1986 - Fourteen people die in a blaze at a garment factory in the Kwai Chung port district.
1986 - A Christmas blaze guts 150 vessels moored in an Aberdeen typhoon shelter on Hong Kong Island, leaving more than 1,700 boat dwellers homeless and virtually penniless. Only two injured.
1990 - Triad gangsters fire-bomb a restaurant and mahjong parlour in Hunghom, killing six and injuring 24.
1990 - Six die and 50 are injured in a fire in a "cage home" slum hostel in Shamshuipo.
1992 - A blaze at the Shek Kong Vietnamese refugee detention centre kills 26 and injures 126.
1994 - A fire-bomb at the Shek Pik Mei branch of a Hong Kong bank kills 12 bank employees.
1996 - A February dry season brush fire traps schoolchildren hiking at Pat Sin Leng in the New Territories. Three pupils and two teachers die and many are permanently burned.

1996 - On November 20, the Garley Building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turns into a towering inferno, killing 39 people and injuring 81. It is the worst building fire recorded in the British colony.
1997 - On January 25, a blaze caused by arson in a karaoke bar kills 17 people in the Tsimshatsui red light district.
1997 - On April 8, a blaze believed caused by a cigarette butt breaks out in a Kowloon residential block. The initial toll is seven dead, including two baby girls, and 28 injured.
